description: The official monitoring dashboard for the Itential Platform deployed on-premises, leveraging Prometheus. To use this dashboard, select your Prometheus datasource from the dropdown. Tabs: Overview, Workflow Engine, Platform Process, Redis, MongoDB.

panels.description: Aggregate reachability of all Itential Platform app nodes (up{job=iap_exporter}). UP = every node up; DEGRADED = at least one node down while others still serve; DOWN = all nodes unreachable — check the app service and the :3443 metrics endpoint on the affected node(s).
panels.title: Itential Platform Application

panels.description: WorkFlowEngine metrics exporter health (itential_up). UP = all WFE exporters up; DEGRADED = some up; DOWN = none exporting job/task metrics — jobs may still run but are unobserved.
panels.title: Workflow Engine

panels.description: Redis (Sentinel master/replica) cluster health. UP = a master is present, all selected nodes are up, and every replica's replication link is healthy. DEGRADED = master present but a node is down or a replica's link to the master is broken. DOWN = no reachable master (job-queue writes failing) — check Sentinel and the Redis tab.

targets.expr: ((count(redis_instance_info{job="redis_exporter",role="master"}) >= bool 1) or vector(0)) * (1 + (min(redis_up{job="redis_exporter"}) == bool 1) * ((min(redis_master_link_up{job="redis_exporter"}) == bool 1) or vector(1)))

panels.title: Redis

panels.description: MongoDB replica-set health. UP = a primary is elected and every data-bearing member is reachable. DEGRADED = primary up but a member is unhealthy (replication still works). DOWN = no primary elected (writes failing) — Itential Platform loses its primary datastore. Hidden/backup members excluded; see the MongoDB tab.
panels.title: MongoDB

panels.description: Jobs currently in progress (status running/paused), read from MongoDB by the WFE exporter — matches Operations Manager > Active Jobs. Reads 0 when idle. A sustained climb alongside rising datastore latency indicates back-pressure.
panels.title: Active Jobs

panels.description: Share of started jobs that error (5m). Normal ≤2%. 2–10% warning, >10% critical — drill into Workflow Engine tab and correlate with datastore health.
panels.title: Job Error Rate

panels.description: Active Itential Platform user/API sessions (iap_active_sessions). Context for load correlation.
panels.title: Active Sessions

panels.description:
Answers: what is the overall platform task completion rate right now?

Sum of completion rates across all nodes. Use as a platform-wide health indicator.

- Rising: the platform is processing more work
- Stable: consistent throughput
- Falling or near zero: throughput has dropped — check individual nodes for failures or idle state
panels.title: Total Task Throughput

panels.description: Per-node CPU busy % (100 - idle rate). Normal ≤60%. >80% sustained indicates CPU pressure on an Itential Platform/datastore node.
panels.title: Node CPU Busy %

panels.description: Per-node memory used % (1 - MemAvailable/MemTotal). Normal ≤70%. >85% risks OOM/swap.
panels.title: Node RAM Used %

panels.description: Per-node, per-mount disk used %. Normal ≤80%. >90% is critical — a full disk on a Mongo/Redis/Itential Platform node causes write failures and outages (the datastore mount, e.g. /var/lib/mongo, matters most).
panels.title: Node Disk Used %

panels.description: Job lifecycle events/sec (5m): started, completed, errored, cancelled. Errored trending up while started is flat signals failures.
panels.title: Job Rates

panels.description: Completed vs started (5m). Normal ≥95%. 80–95% warning, <80% critical.
panels.title: Job Success Rate

panels.description: Jobs currently running/paused (from MongoDB), over time. Reads 0 when idle; peaks show concurrent job load. Sustained high in-progress with rising datastore latency indicates back-pressure. Matches Operations Manager > Active Jobs.
panels.title: Jobs In Progress

panels.description: Count of job documents retained in MongoDB by final status — the composition of the jobs collection. Large complete/canceled counts reflect retention policy; a growing error count warrants investigation. The legacy 'cancelled' spelling (9,446 old records from a prior Itential Platform version) is folded into 'canceled' here so the total is accurate.
panels.title: Job Records by Status (MongoDB)

panels.description: Tasks started/sec (line) vs completed/sec (filled area), 5m. When the started line rises above the completed area, that visible gap is work queuing faster than it finishes — the overload signal. Under healthy load the line sits on top of the fill. Tasks are the steps within jobs.
panels.title: Task Start vs Complete

panels.description: Share of tasks started by each Itential Platform server (server_id) over the selected time range — slices sum to the cluster total, and the legend shows each server's task count and percentage. A lopsided split means task load is not evenly balanced across nodes. Reacts to the dashboard time picker. Task metrics carry server_id; job metrics are cluster-aggregate only.
panels.title: Task Distribution by Server

panels.description: Total tasks started across all Itential Platform servers over the selected time range — the sum of the donut's slices. Reacts to the dashboard time picker.
panels.title: Total Tasks

panels.description: Task errors/sec (5m). Normal ≈0. >0.1/s warrants investigation into a failing workflow or adapter.
panels.title: Task Error Rate

panels.description: WFE watcher reconnects in the last hour (itential_watcher_reconnects_total). Repeated reconnects hint at datastore/network instability.
panels.title: Watcher Reconnects (1h)

panels.description: Distinct Pronghorn Application processes running (excludes adapters and the Core init process).
panels.title: Applications

panels.description: Distinct Pronghorn Adapter processes running (integrations to external systems).
panels.title: Adapters

panels.description: Combined resident memory (RSS) of all Pronghorn Application processes across Itential Platform nodes.
panels.title: Applications Memory

panels.description: Combined resident memory (RSS) of all Pronghorn Adapter processes across Itential Platform nodes.
panels.title: Adapters Memory

panels.description: Combined thread count across all Pronghorn processes (Core + Applications + Adapters). A sudden jump can indicate a runaway component.
panels.title: Total Threads

panels.description: Combined open file descriptors across all Pronghorn processes. Steady growth signals an FD leak (sockets/files not closed).
panels.title: Total Open FDs

panels.description: Node.js V8 heap utilization % per Itential Platform instance. Normal ≤70%. Sustained >85% precedes GC pressure and event-loop stalls.
panels.title: V8 Heap Used %

panels.description: V8 heap used vs total allocated per Itential Platform instance (bytes). Used approaching total means the heap is saturating.
panels.title: Heap Used vs Total

panels.description: Itential Platform process CPU usage split user vs system per instance. A system-heavy profile suggests I/O or syscall pressure.
panels.title: Process CPU (User / System)

panels.description: Top 10 Pronghorn Application processes by CPU seconds/sec (5m). Identifies which platform application is burning CPU.
panels.title: Top Applications by CPU

panels.description: Top 10 Pronghorn Application processes by resident memory (bytes). Identifies memory-heavy platform applications.
panels.title: Top Applications by Memory

panels.description: Top 10 Pronghorn Adapter processes by CPU seconds/sec (5m). Identifies which integration adapter is burning CPU.
panels.title: Top Adapters by CPU

panels.description: Top 10 Pronghorn Adapter processes by resident memory (bytes). Identifies memory-heavy integration adapters.
panels.title: Top Adapters by Memory

panels.description: Per-component resource usage across Itential Platform nodes — classified as Core (the main/init process), Application, or Adapter. CPU (% of one core), memory as % of node RAM and absolute RSS, thread and file-descriptor counts, and process uptime. Sorted by memory share; a component missing from the list is not running. Heat cells go green→red with load, and a steadily climbing RSS or FD count on one row points to a leak.

targets.expr: sum by (groupname, instance) (label_replace(sum by (groupname, instance)(namedprocess_namegroup_memory_bytes{groupname=~"Pronghorn.*",memtype="resident",instance=~"$node(:.*)?"}), "host", "$1", "instance", "([^:]+).*") * 100 / on(host) group_left() label_replace(node_memory_MemTotal_bytes{job="node_exporter",instance=~"$node(:.*)?"}, "host", "$1", "instance", "([^:]+).*"))

panels.title: Component Resource Detail

panels.description: Every Redis data node with its role (master/replica), reachability, and — for replicas — the health of the replication link to the master. Health green = node UP; Master Link green = replica is in sync with its master (N/A on the master itself). Exactly one master is expected; Sentinel nodes are excluded. One row per node.
panels.title: Cluster Members

panels.description: Connected vs blocked Redis clients per instance. Blocked clients are worker processes waiting on job queues; a rising blocked count signals queue back-pressure.
panels.title: Clients (Connected / Blocked)

panels.description: Used memory per instance vs configured maxmemory (0 = unlimited). Approaching max triggers eviction.
panels.title: Memory Used vs Max

panels.description: Rate of the Redis operations Itential Platform uses to move messages through its job queues (5m): brpoplpush/rpoplpush move jobs waiting→active, zpopmin promotes delayed jobs, xadd publishes queue events, lpush/rpush enqueue. Itential Platform uses Redis as a message broker (not a cache), so this is the broker's message-exchange throughput. A sustained drop to ~0 while jobs are pending points to stalled workers.
panels.title: Queue Operations

panels.description: Average server-side latency of the non-blocking job-queue operations (5m) — enqueue (lpush/rpush), job move (rpoplpush), delayed-job promotion (zpopmin), event publish (xadd). Blocking waits (brpoplpush) are excluded, since their duration is mostly idle time waiting for a job rather than broker load. Normal is well under 1 ms; a sustained climb means Redis is becoming a bottleneck for message exchange.
panels.title: Queue Operation Latency

panels.description: Commands processed per second per instance (5m). Baseline for load; sudden spikes correlate with job bursts.
panels.title: Commands / sec

panels.description: Key count per instance (sum over DBs). Unbounded growth may indicate keys without TTL.
panels.title: Total Keys

panels.description: Connected replicas and replica lag (seconds). Lag series only report on replica instances; none on the primary is expected.
panels.title: Replication

panels.description: Redis network throughput in/out (bytes/sec, 5m).
panels.title: Network I/O

panels.description: Evicted keys/sec and rejected connections/sec (5m). Any sustained eviction means memory pressure; rejections mean maxclients hit.
panels.title: Evictions & Rejected Connections

panels.description: Every replica-set member with role and health (green = UP, red = DOWN), one row per member. Only PRIMARY/SECONDARY members are shown; an optional backup/hidden node is intentionally excluded.
panels.title: Cluster Members

panels.description: Overall replica-set health. Healthy = a primary is elected and every data-bearing member is reachable. Degraded = primary up but a member is unhealthy (one node failed — replication still works). Down = no primary elected (writes are failing). Optional hidden/backup members are not counted.
panels.title: Replica Set Status

panels.description: Secondary replication lag behind the primary (seconds), derived from member optime. Normal <10s. 10–60s warning, ≥60s critical. Hidden/backup members are excluded.

targets.expr: (max by (rs_nm) (mongodb_rs_members_optimeDate{member_state="PRIMARY"}) - on (rs_nm) group_right avg by (rs_nm, member_idx) (mongodb_rs_members_optimeDate{member_state="SECONDARY"})) / 1000

panels.title: Replication Lag

panels.description: Operations/sec by type (insert/query/update/delete/getmore/command, 5m). The workload profile of the replica set.
panels.title: Operation Rates

panels.description: Current vs available connections per instance. Current approaching available risks connection exhaustion.
panels.title: Connections

panels.description: Current WiredTiger cache utilization of the busiest MongoDB node — the max across the replica set. Green <80%, yellow 80–95%, red ≥95%. At-a-glance companion to the trend on the right: if this is red, the working set no longer fits in cache and MongoDB is reading from disk.
panels.title: Cache Utilization (peak)

panels.description: How full the WiredTiger cache is per node — bytes currently in cache vs the configured maximum. WiredTiger holds MongoDB's working set here. Normal is under 80%. 80–95% means the cache is filling and eviction pressure is rising; ≥95% means the working set no longer fits, so MongoDB churns cache and reads from disk (slower queries). If this stays high, add RAM or raise the WiredTiger cache size.
panels.title: WiredTiger Cache Utilization

panels.description: MongoDB page faults per second per node (rate of extra_info.page_faults) — MongoDB fetching data from disk because it wasn't in memory. Normal is near 0 with a warm cache. A sustained rise means the working set no longer fits in RAM and reads are hitting disk; correlate with WiredTiger Cache Utilization and consider adding RAM.
panels.title: Page Faults

title: Itential Platform Monitoring
